behavior: Active foliage gleaner that forages especially among outer treetop branches, probing and picking insects, hovering at foliage, and sallying for flying prey. It also takes nectar, sap, and fruit, migrates mainly at night, and is territorial during the breeding season.
field_marks: Small, delicate warbler with a short tail
Slender, dark, slightly downcurved bill and dark eye
Yellow underparts marked with narrow dark “tiger” streaks
Adult male has a chestnut cheek framed by yellow; females and immatures are duller with a grayish cheek
Olive upperparts and dark wings with a conspicuous white patch or wingbars
Dark, slender legs and white undertail coverts
habitat: Breeds in mature boreal forests dominated by spruce and balsam fir, often near openings or forest edges. During migration it uses varied woodland, scrub, and thickets; nonbreeding habitats include shrubby plantings, second growth, pine and broadleaf forest, dry forest, and mangroves.
